title: Monitoring
description: Live health of platform services, queues and institute activity.

dlq.banner: {count, plural, one {# failed event is} other {# failed events are}} waiting in the dead letter queue: what they should have done (a notification, a billing change, an audit entry) has not happened.

alerts.heading: Active alerts
alerts.unavailable: Alerts cannot be shown: the metrics store (OpenObserve) does not answer. Open Observability to check it; alerts appear here again once it answers.
alerts.recovered: Recovered, closing at the next check

notification_service_down.title: Notification service stopped
notification_service_down.impact: No message is going out on any channel (e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp, push) while it is stopped.
notification_service_down.step1: Check the notification service under "Services" above.
notification_service_down.step2: Read the service's log in Observability: it names why the worker stopped, and it retries every 30 seconds.
notification_service_down.step3: Check that Temporal is reachable and that at least one instance runs the worker.

notification_canary_missing.title: Test message not delivered
notification_canary_missing.impact: The platform's test message has not been accepted on this channel for over 30 minutes. Real messages on this channel are probably not arriving.
notification_canary_missing.step1: Open "Notification delivery" below: check when the test message was last accepted and how many sends failed.
notification_canary_missing.step2: Open "WhatsApp senders": a sender marked blocked or paused is the cause.
notification_canary_missing.step3: If both look normal, follow the runbook: the provider's status, then the notification service's log.

notification_failure_rate.title: Many messages failing
notification_failure_rate.impact: More than 1 in 5 messages on this channel failed in the last 10 minutes. People are missing messages now.
notification_failure_rate.step1: Open "Notification delivery" below to see the failed count per channel.
notification_failure_rate.step2: In Observability, find the failure reason of the failed sends: one reason for most of them points at the provider or its credentials.

notification_sender_blocked.title: WhatsApp number blocked
notification_sender_blocked.impact: The provider blocked a WhatsApp number. Nothing is sent from it; institutes that use it fall back to the platform's number when that one is active.
notification_sender_blocked.step1: Open "WhatsApp senders" below to see which number is blocked.
notification_sender_blocked.step2: Resolve the restriction in the provider's console.
notification_sender_blocked.step3: Activate the sender again; the alert ends then.

notification_breaker_opened.title: Sending paused on a provider
notification_breaker_opened.impact: A provider or a WhatsApp number kept failing, so sending through it is paused and retried every minute. Messages wait; none are lost.
notification_breaker_opened.step1: Open "Notification delivery" below to see which channel is failing.
notification_breaker_opened.step2: Check the provider's status page and the credentials of that channel.
notification_breaker_opened.step3: It ends by itself when a retry succeeds.

notification_events_stuck.title: Notification events waiting
notification_events_stuck.impact: Events that start notifications have waited over 5 minutes. Messages are late.
notification_events_stuck.step1: Check the notification service under "Services" above and in its log.
notification_events_stuck.step2: Look at the NOTIFICATION stream in "Queue backlog (NATS)".
notification_events_stuck.step3: A handler that keeps failing holds its queue until the event is dead-lettered.

notification_dead_letters.title: A notification was never sent
notification_dead_letters.impact: A notification event failed every retry and was set aside, so its message did not go out.
notification_dead_letters.step1: Open the Dead Letter Queue and find the NOTIFICATION message.
notification_dead_letters.step2: Read its error and fix the cause.
notification_dead_letters.step3: Replay it from there; sending it twice is safe.

notification_skips_rising.title: Messages skipped: channel not set up
notification_skips_rising.impact: Messages on this channel were skipped because it has no provider or the message has no approved template. Recipients on this channel get nothing.
notification_skips_rising.step1: Open "Notification delivery" below to see which channel is affected.
notification_skips_rising.step2: For no_provider: set the channel's provider, and for WhatsApp activate a sender. For no_template: register or approve the template with the provider.
notification_skips_rising.step3: It ends 15 minutes after the last skip.

dlq_messages_warning.title: Events failing and set aside
dlq_messages_warning.impact: More than one event a minute is failing every retry. What it should have done (a notification, a billing change, an audit entry) did not happen.
dlq_messages_warning.step1: Open the Dead Letter Queue and read the subject and error of the newest messages.
dlq_messages_warning.step2: Fix the cause, then replay them.
dlq_messages_warning.step3: Follow the runbook if they keep coming.

dlq_messages_critical.title: Many events failing and set aside
dlq_messages_critical.impact: More than 10 events a minute are failing every retry. Notifications, billing changes or audit entries are being lost now.
dlq_messages_critical.step1: Open the Dead Letter Queue and read the subject and error of the newest messages.
dlq_messages_critical.step2: Fix the cause, then replay them.
dlq_messages_critical.step3: Follow the runbook if they keep coming.

eventbus_emit_failures_warning.title: Events not being published
eventbus_emit_failures_warning.impact: The gateway cannot publish events to the message broker. Notifications, billing and audit steps after a change are being missed.
eventbus_emit_failures_warning.step2: Read the gateway's log in Observability for the failing subject.
eventbus_emit_failures_warning.step3: Follow the runbook for a missing or changed stream.

eventbus_emit_failures_critical.title: Many events not being published
eventbus_emit_failures_critical.impact: The gateway is failing to publish more than 10 events a minute. Notifications, billing and audit steps after a change are being lost now.
eventbus_emit_failures_critical.step2: Read the gateway's log in Observability for the failing subject.
eventbus_emit_failures_critical.step3: Follow the runbook for a missing or changed stream.

audit_consumer_lag.title: Audit log falling behind
audit_consumer_lag.impact: Over 30 audit events have waited 5 minutes to be written. The audit log is incomplete until they are.
audit_consumer_lag.step1: Look at the AUDIT stream in "Queue backlog (NATS)".
audit_consumer_lag.step2: Check the gateway and the database under "Services" above.
audit_consumer_lag.step3: Read the audit consumer's log in Observability.

audit_dlq_depth.title: Audit entries dropped
audit_dlq_depth.impact: Audit events failed every retry: some actions are missing from the audit log.
audit_dlq_depth.step1: Open the Dead Letter Queue and find the AUDIT messages.
audit_dlq_depth.step2: Read the audit consumer's log for the error and fix the cause.
audit_dlq_depth.step3: Replay them from the Dead Letter Queue.

audit_event_spike.title: Unusual amount of activity
audit_event_spike.impact: Audit events in the last hour are over three times the usual hourly amount. This can be a bulk change or deletion.
audit_event_spike.step1: Open the audit log and look at the last hour: who made the changes, and where.
audit_event_spike.step2: Confirm with that person or institute that the change was intended.

audit_impersonation_volume.title: Many actions while impersonating
audit_impersonation_volume.impact: More than 10 actions were taken while impersonating users in one scope in the last hour.
audit_impersonation_volume.step1: Open impersonation sessions and check who impersonated whom, and why.
audit_impersonation_volume.step2: End any session that is not expected.

audit_partition_creation.title: Audit log may stop at month end
audit_partition_creation.impact: It is late in the month and no audit event has been written, so next month's audit table may not be ready.
audit_partition_creation.step1: Read the audit consumer's log in Observability.
audit_partition_creation.step2: Check the audit partition workflow in Temporal.

notification_template_rejected.title: WhatsApp template cannot be sent
notification_template_rejected.impact: The provider refused, paused or switched off a WhatsApp template on an account, or has not reviewed it in two days. Alerts that use it are not sent from that account.
notification_template_rejected.step1: Open "WhatsApp senders" below and open Templates on the sender: it names the template and the reason.
notification_template_rejected.step2: Fix the wording under a new name, then press Sync now.
notification_template_rejected.step3: A paused template comes back by itself when its quality improves. For one still waiting after two days, ask the provider about its review.

notification_template_changed.title: WhatsApp template changed by the provider
notification_template_changed.impact: The provider approved a template under another category, or its text was edited at the provider. A recategorised template is not sent.
notification_template_changed.step1: Open "WhatsApp senders" below and open Templates on the sender to see which template changed.
notification_template_changed.step2: Reword it under a new name so it says what it is about for the reader, then press Sync now.

api_foreign_scope_response.title: A response was refused: it carried another institute's data
api_foreign_scope_response.impact: The API was about to answer an institute or reseller with a row that belongs to someone else, and stopped. The caller saw an error; a fault in the code let the row get that far.
api_foreign_scope_response.step1: Open the logs and search the api-gateway for "outside the caller's scope" to find the operation.
api_foreign_scope_response.step2: Follow the runbook: record it as a security finding and fix the operation.
